issues.legal_issue: An endowment is a public religious trust when the public has an interest in it, including where outsiders exercise supervisory control over its management.
material_facts: The founders dedicated properties to the idol and completely divested themselves of title to or interest in those properties.
The founders’ family retained the right to provide the shebait or manager, but outsiders were given power to supervise the shebait and remove him for improper management.
The temple stood within separate compound walls, apart from the founders’ residential premises.
The documents provided for the appointment and dismissal of pujaris, and members of the public worshipped at the temple.
issues.conclusion: The endowment was a religious trust because the public was interested in it; the appeal was allowed and the trial court’s judgment was restored.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 2(g) of the Bihar Hindu Religious Trusts Act, public interest in a trust may be shown by public association with the management. Where properties are endowed directly to an idol, public use of the temple without interference is cogent evidence of dedication for the public. The court followed Deoki Nandan v. Murlidhar (1956 SCR 756), explained Bhagwan Din v. Har Saroop (AIR 1940 PC 7) and Ramsaran Das v. Jai Ram Das (AIR 1943 Pat 135), and noted that Deoki Nandan had referred to the separate location of a place of worship as a relevant factor, citing Delroos Banoo Begum v. Nawab Syud Ashgur Ally Khan (1875 15 Bom. L.R. 167). The statutory word is “ministration,” not “administration.”

rule.if: religious_endowment_status_case and properties_dedicated_to_idol and founders_divested_property_interest and outsiders_could_supervise_and_remove_manager

predicates.religious_endowment_status_case: The proceeding concerns whether an endowment for a place of worship is public or private.
predicates.properties_dedicated_to_idol: The founders dedicated properties directly to an idol.
predicates.founders_divested_property_interest: The founders gave up their title to and interest in the dedicated properties.
predicates.outsiders_could_supervise_and_remove_man: People outside the founders’ family were empowered to supervise the manager and remove him for improper management.
predicates.endowment_is_public_religious_trust: The endowment is treated as a public religious trust.

issues.definition: When a religious endowment case concerns properties dedicated to an idol, the founders have relinquished their property interests, and outsiders can supervise and remove the manager, the endowment is treated as a public religious trust.
